questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In the Prologue, what form of poem does Shakespeare use to open the play?
questions.why: The Prologue is written as a 14-line sonnet, spoken by the Chorus to set up the story before the action begins.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In C–Am–F–G, which chord sits between Am and G in the sequence?
questions.why: The progression runs C, then Am, then F, then G — F is the third chord, sitting right between Am and G.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.prompt: In 'Paint Like a Beast', what was the main artistic goal?
questions.why: The activities aimed at bold, expressive texture and movement, not photo-realism — a common mix-up is thinking 'good art' means precise, smooth detail.
options: Blending edges for a soft look

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these steps of how a shogun kept control of Japan, from first to last
sequence: Samurai enforce order and collect loyalty
Peasants farm the land for daimyo
questions.why: The shogun granted land to daimyo in exchange for loyalty, daimyo relied on samurai to enforce their rule, and peasants worked the land at the bottom of the system.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these steps of a continuity-and-change argument, from first to last
questions.why: A strong continuity-and-change argument first sets out the earlier situation, then the later one, then pinpoints the actual change, and finally explains its significance.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Act 1, who does Romeo ask to help him sneak into the Capulet party?
questions.why: Benvolio persuades Romeo to go to the party uninvited so he can compare Rosaline to other girls — a key setup for meeting Juliet.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which theatre was strongly associated with Shakespeare's plays?
questions.why: The Globe Theatre in London was built by Shakespeare's acting company and staged many of his plays, including Romeo and Juliet.
